It lists refs from an earlier cross-reference list, by tier, that your refs do not include. ===== _commentary/v16/prompts/map3/surah_map.md (adapted) =====
Read the surah as one text and write its map of image chains: the lexical images that run through several of
its ayat and join them into one scene, process or movement. A later writer will read one ayah at a time, with
only that ayah's own dictionary. The map lets that writer hear what the ayah's words carry in the surah as a
whole, including senses whose evidence sits under the words of other ayat.

Your evidence is the surah text, the dictionary of every root in the surah (each branch with the classical
dictionaries' own phrases), an earlier reader's channel review (channels.md),
and your own knowledge of Arabic and the Quran. Where a member or passage comes from memory rather than from
the dictionary or the text, say so. Do not delegate, browse or inspect files; run only the command the header describes.

The channel review is an earlier reader's proposal. Ignore its judgements: grades,
strength or confidence labels, reading types, words such as "surprising", "exploratory" or "latent", and every
statement of what a reading may or may not do. Make your own judgement from the surah's words, the dictionary
phrases and the Quran. Do not rediscover what it already assembled: start from its chains, test each one
against the dictionary phrases and the text, and join, extend, split or correct them. Where its wording
abstracts a member, go back to the dictionary phrase and name what it actually says.

A chain belongs on the map when its members are senses the dictionary attests for words that stand in the surah,
and together they make one image or process that the surah's wording or sequence lets a listener hear. A member
need not be the sense that translates its word in its own ayah; a chain is heard across the surah, not in one
word. A chain may join a sense and its reversal as well as the parts of one scene. Mark a member attested only
inside a fixed expression [fixed expression]; add no other label to a member or a chain, and where a source
records a phrase and rejects it, say so of that phrase alone. When the dictionary itself joins two of the
surah's words in one phrase, quote that phrase: it is the strongest evidence a chain can have. Keep a scene at
the level of its objects, their parts and their operation. When proposals share members, do not fold one into
another's more abstract function unless nothing concrete is lost. Carry every chain that meets this test,
however unusual; leave out proposals that do not.

Write the map in English, with Arabic quoted exactly (surah wording from the text, dictionary phrases from the
dictionary). It is working material for the writer, not commentary prose.

1. `## Chains`. For each chain, a `###` heading naming the image. One paragraph on what the image is and how it
   moves through the surah. Then its members, one line each: the ayah ref, the word as it stands in the text,
   the root and branch id, the dictionary's own phrase quoted exactly, and what this member contributes to the
   image. Add Quran passages outside the surah, with exact refs, where they stage or confirm the chain; for
   each, name the speaker and the situation in a few words, and include the ayah that opens its scene when the
   passage continues one.
2. `## Interactions`. Where chains meet: a shared member, a dictionary phrase that joins members of two chains,
   a Quran passage that stages two chains together, or one chain's scene needing another's. One line each: the
   chains, where they meet, the evidence.
3. `## Ayat`. For each ayah in order: the chains its words take part in, what its words add to each, and in one
   line the whole scene each chain makes across the surah, so that a writer who sees only this ayah sees the
   scene, not a fragment.
4. `## Not carried`. Each channel subchannel you did not carry into a chain: one short line
   each, its name and why, no prose.

No ranking and no labels of strength or confidence. No list of what a writer must include. There is no length
target and no required number of chains or members.

===== _commentary/v16/work/s024/surah.r2/text.md =====
# Surah 24

- 24:1 سُورَةٌ أَنزَلْنَٰهَا وَفَرَضْنَٰهَا وَأَنزَلْنَا فِيهَآ ءَايَٰتٍۭ بَيِّنَٰتٍۢ لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ
- 24:2 ٱلزَّانِيَةُ وَٱلزَّانِى فَٱجْلِدُوا۟ كُلَّ وَٰحِدٍۢ مِّنْهُمَا مِا۟ئَةَ جَلْدَةٍۢ ۖ وَلَا تَأْخُذْكُم بِهِمَا رَأْفَةٌۭ فِى دِينِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ تُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ ۖ وَلْيَشْهَدْ عَذَابَهُمَا طَآئِفَةٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
- 24:3 ٱلزَّانِى لَا يَنكِحُ إِلَّا زَانِيَةً أَوْ مُشْرِكَةًۭ وَٱلزَّانِيَةُ لَا يَنكِحُهَآ إِلَّا زَانٍ أَوْ مُشْرِكٌۭ ۚ وَحُرِّمَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
- 24:4 وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ ٱلْمُحْصَنَٰتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُوا۟ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَ فَٱجْلِدُوهُمْ ثَمَٰنِينَ جَلْدَةًۭ وَلَا تَقْبَلُوا۟ لَهُمْ شَهَٰدَةً أَبَدًۭا ۚ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَٰسِقُونَ
- 24:5 إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ تَابُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ وَأَصْلَحُوا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
- 24:6 وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أَزْوَٰجَهُمْ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُمْ شُهَدَآءُ إِلَّآ أَنفُسُهُمْ فَشَهَٰدَةُ أَحَدِهِمْ أَرْبَعُ شَهَٰدَٰتٍۭ بِٱللَّهِ ۙ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
- 24:7 وَٱلْخَٰمِسَةُ أَنَّ لَعْنَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
- 24:8 وَيَدْرَؤُا۟ عَنْهَا ٱلْعَذَابَ أَن تَشْهَدَ أَرْبَعَ شَهَٰدَٰتٍۭ بِٱللَّهِ ۙ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
- 24:9 وَٱلْخَٰمِسَةَ أَنَّ غَضَبَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهَآ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
- 24:10 وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُۥ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ حَكِيمٌ
- 24:11 إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو بِٱلْإِفْكِ عُصْبَةٌۭ مِّنكُمْ ۚ لَا تَحْسَبُوهُ شَرًّۭا لَّكُم ۖ بَلْ هُوَ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكُمْ ۚ لِكُلِّ ٱمْرِئٍۢ مِّنْهُم مَّا ٱكْتَسَبَ مِنَ ٱلْإِثْمِ ۚ وَٱلَّذِى تَوَلَّىٰ كِبْرَهُۥ مِنْهُمْ لَهُۥ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌۭ
- 24:12 لَّوْلَآ إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتُ بِأَنفُسِهِمْ خَيْرًۭا وَقَالُوا۟ هَٰذَآ إِفْكٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
- 24:13 لَّوْلَا جَآءُو عَلَيْهِ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَ ۚ فَإِذْ لَمْ يَأْتُوا۟ بِٱلشُّهَدَآءِ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُمُ ٱلْكَٰذِبُونَ
- 24:14 وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُۥ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ لَمَسَّكُمْ فِى مَآ أَفَضْتُمْ فِيهِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
- 24:15 إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُۥ بِأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ وَتَقُولُونَ بِأَفْوَاهِكُم مَّا لَيْسَ لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلْمٌۭ وَتَحْسَبُونَهُۥ هَيِّنًۭا وَهُوَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمٌۭ
- 24:16 وَلَوْلَآ إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ قُلْتُم مَّا يَكُونُ لَنَآ أَن نَّتَكَلَّمَ بِهَٰذَا سُبْحَٰنَكَ هَٰذَا بُهْتَٰنٌ عَظِيمٌۭ
- 24:17 يَعِظُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ أَن تَعُودُوا۟ لِمِثْلِهِۦٓ أَبَدًا إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
- 24:18 وَيُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ
- 24:19 إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحِبُّونَ أَن تَشِيعَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةُ فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۭ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
- 24:20 وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُۥ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَءُوفٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
- 24:21 ۞ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ خُطُوَٰتِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ۚ وَمَن يَتَّبِعْ خُطُوَٰتِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ ۚ وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُۥ مَا زَكَىٰ مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَدًۭا وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُزَكِّى مَن يَشَآءُ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌۭ
- 24:22 وَلَا يَأْتَلِ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْفَضْلِ مِنكُمْ وَٱلسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤْتُوٓا۟ أُو۟لِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱلْمُهَٰجِرِينَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَلْيَعْفُوا۟ وَلْيَصْفَحُوٓا۟ ۗ أَلَا تُحِبُّونَ أَن يَغْفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌ
- 24:23 إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ ٱلْمُحْصَنَٰتِ ٱلْغَٰفِلَٰتِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ لُعِنُوا۟ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌۭ
- 24:24 يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَلْسِنَتُهُمْ وَأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُم بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
- 24:25 يَوْمَئِذٍۢ يُوَفِّيهِمُ ٱللَّهُ دِينَهُمُ ٱلْحَقَّ وَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْحَقُّ ٱلْمُبِينُ
- 24:26 ٱلْخَبِيثَٰتُ لِلْخَبِيثِينَ وَٱلْخَبِيثُونَ لِلْخَبِيثَٰتِ ۖ وَٱلطَّيِّبَٰتُ لِلطَّيِّبِينَ وَٱلطَّيِّبُونَ لِلطَّيِّبَٰتِ ۚ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ مُبَرَّءُونَ مِمَّا يَقُولُونَ ۖ لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌۭ وَرِزْقٌۭ كَرِيمٌۭ
- 24:27 يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَدْخُلُوا۟ بُيُوتًا غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ حَتَّىٰ تَسْتَأْنِسُوا۟ وَتُسَلِّمُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهَا ۚ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ
- 24:28 فَإِن لَّمْ تَجِدُوا۟ فِيهَآ أَحَدًۭا فَلَا تَدْخُلُوهَا حَتَّىٰ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ ۖ وَإِن قِيلَ لَكُمُ ٱرْجِعُوا۟ فَٱرْجِعُوا۟ ۖ هُوَ أَزْكَىٰ لَكُمْ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِيمٌۭ
- 24:29 لَّيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَدْخُلُوا۟ بُيُوتًا غَيْرَ مَسْكُونَةٍۢ فِيهَا مَتَٰعٌۭ لَّكُمْ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا تَكْتُمُونَ
- 24:30 قُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا۟ مِنْ أَبْصَٰرِهِمْ وَيَحْفَظُوا۟ فُرُوجَهُمْ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَزْكَىٰ لَهُمْ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا يَصْنَعُونَ
- 24:31 وَقُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحْفَظْنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا ۖ وَلْيَضْرِبْنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّ ۖ وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ أَبْنَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ أَبْنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ إِخْوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوْ بَنِىٓ إِخْوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوْ بَنِىٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوْ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ ٱلتَّٰبِعِينَ غَيْرِ أُو۟لِى ٱلْإِرْبَةِ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ أَوِ ٱلطِّفْلِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يَظْهَرُوا۟ عَلَىٰ عَوْرَٰتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ ۖ وَلَا يَضْرِبْنَ بِأَرْجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعْلَمَ مَا يُخْفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّ ۚ وَتُوبُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ
- 24:32 وَأَنكِحُوا۟ ٱلْأَيَٰمَىٰ مِنكُمْ وَٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ مِنْ عِبَادِكُمْ وَإِمَآئِكُمْ ۚ إِن يَكُونُوا۟ فُقَرَآءَ يُغْنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌۭ
- 24:33 وَلْيَسْتَعْفِفِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا حَتَّىٰ يُغْنِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ ۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبْتَغُونَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُكُمْ فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًۭا ۖ وَءَاتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ ءَاتَىٰكُمْ ۚ وَلَا تُكْرِهُوا۟ فَتَيَٰتِكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْبِغَآءِ إِنْ أَرَدْنَ تَحَصُّنًۭا لِّتَبْتَغُوا۟ عَرَضَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا ۚ وَمَن يُكْرِههُّنَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ إِكْرَٰهِهِنَّ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
- 24:34 وَلَقَدْ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكُمْ ءَايَٰتٍۢ مُّبَيِّنَٰتٍۢ وَمَثَلًۭا مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوْا۟ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَمَوْعِظَةًۭ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
- 24:35 ۞ ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ مَثَلُ نُورِهِۦ كَمِشْكَوٰةٍۢ فِيهَا مِصْبَاحٌ ۖ ٱلْمِصْبَاحُ فِى زُجَاجَةٍ ۖ ٱلزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوْكَبٌۭ دُرِّىٌّۭ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةٍۢ مُّبَٰرَكَةٍۢ زَيْتُونَةٍۢ لَّا شَرْقِيَّةٍۢ وَلَا غَرْبِيَّةٍۢ يَكَادُ زَيْتُهَا يُضِىٓءُ وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌۭ ۚ نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍۢ ۗ يَهْدِى ٱللَّهُ لِنُورِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَيَضْرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْأَمْثَٰلَ لِلنَّاسِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌۭ
- 24:36 فِى بُيُوتٍ أَذِنَ ٱللَّهُ أَن تُرْفَعَ وَيُذْكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسْمُهُۥ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ فِيهَا بِٱلْغُدُوِّ وَٱلْءَاصَالِ
- 24:37 رِجَالٌۭ لَّا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَٰرَةٌۭ وَلَا بَيْعٌ عَن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ وَإِقَامِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَإِيتَآءِ ٱلزَّكَوٰةِ ۙ يَخَافُونَ يَوْمًۭا تَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ
- 24:38 لِيَجْزِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ أَحْسَنَ مَا عَمِلُوا۟ وَيَزِيدَهُم مِّن فَضْلِهِۦ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍۢ
- 24:39 وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَعْمَٰلُهُمْ كَسَرَابٍۭ بِقِيعَةٍۢ يَحْسَبُهُ ٱلظَّمْـَٔانُ مَآءً حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَهُۥ لَمْ يَجِدْهُ شَيْـًۭٔا وَوَجَدَ ٱللَّهَ عِندَهُۥ فَوَفَّىٰهُ حِسَابَهُۥ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَرِيعُ ٱلْحِسَابِ
- 24:40 أَوْ كَظُلُمَٰتٍۢ فِى بَحْرٍۢ لُّجِّىٍّۢ يَغْشَىٰهُ مَوْجٌۭ مِّن فَوْقِهِۦ مَوْجٌۭ مِّن فَوْقِهِۦ سَحَابٌۭ ۚ ظُلُمَٰتٌۢ بَعْضُهَا فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ إِذَآ أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُۥ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَىٰهَا ۗ وَمَن لَّمْ يَجْعَلِ ٱللَّهُ لَهُۥ نُورًۭا فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن نُّورٍ
- 24:41 أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱلطَّيْرُ صَٰٓفَّٰتٍۢ ۖ كُلٌّۭ قَدْ عَلِمَ صَلَاتَهُۥ وَتَسْبِيحَهُۥ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌۢ بِمَا يَفْعَلُونَ
- 24:42 وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
- 24:43 أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُزْجِى سَحَابًۭا ثُمَّ يُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُۥ ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُۥ رُكَامًۭا فَتَرَى ٱلْوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلَٰلِهِۦ وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن جِبَالٍۢ فِيهَا مِنۢ بَرَدٍۢ فَيُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَصْرِفُهُۥ عَن مَّن يَشَآءُ ۖ يَكَادُ سَنَا بَرْقِهِۦ يَذْهَبُ بِٱلْأَبْصَٰرِ
- 24:44 يُقَلِّبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَعِبْرَةًۭ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَبْصَٰرِ
- 24:45 وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَآبَّةٍۢ مِّن مَّآءٍۢ ۖ فَمِنْهُم مَّن يَمْشِى عَلَىٰ بَطْنِهِۦ وَمِنْهُم مَّن يَمْشِى عَلَىٰ رِجْلَيْنِ وَمِنْهُم مَّن يَمْشِى عَلَىٰٓ أَرْبَعٍۢ ۚ يَخْلُقُ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌۭ
- 24:46 لَّقَدْ أَنزَلْنَآ ءَايَٰتٍۢ مُّبَيِّنَٰتٍۢ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍۢ مُّسْتَقِيمٍۢ
- 24:47 وَيَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَبِٱلرَّسُولِ وَأَطَعْنَا ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّىٰ فَرِيقٌۭ مِّنْهُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ ۚ وَمَآ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
- 24:48 وَإِذَا دُعُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِذَا فَرِيقٌۭ مِّنْهُم مُّعْرِضُونَ
- 24:49 وَإِن يَكُن لَّهُمُ ٱلْحَقُّ يَأْتُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ مُذْعِنِينَ
- 24:50 أَفِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ أَمِ ٱرْتَابُوٓا۟ أَمْ يَخَافُونَ أَن يَحِيفَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَرَسُولُهُۥ ۚ بَلْ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
- 24:51 إِنَّمَا كَانَ قَوْلَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذَا دُعُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا ۚ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ
- 24:52 وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَيَخْشَ ٱللَّهَ وَيَتَّقْهِ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَآئِزُونَ
- 24:53 ۞ وَأَقْسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَٰنِهِمْ لَئِنْ أَمَرْتَهُمْ لَيَخْرُجُنَّ ۖ قُل لَّا تُقْسِمُوا۟ ۖ طَاعَةٌۭ مَّعْرُوفَةٌ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
- 24:54 قُلْ أَطِيعُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا۟ ٱلرَّسُولَ ۖ فَإِن تَوَلَّوْا۟ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْهِ مَا حُمِّلَ وَعَلَيْكُم مَّا حُمِّلْتُمْ ۖ وَإِن تُطِيعُوهُ تَهْتَدُوا۟ ۚ وَمَا عَلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ إِلَّا ٱلْبَلَٰغُ ٱلْمُبِينُ
- 24:55 وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مِنكُمْ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ كَمَا ٱسْتَخْلَفَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ وَلَيُمَكِّنَنَّ لَهُمْ دِينَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى ٱرْتَضَىٰ لَهُمْ وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ خَوْفِهِمْ أَمْنًۭا ۚ يَعْبُدُونَنِى لَا يُشْرِكُونَ بِى شَيْـًۭٔا ۚ وَمَن كَفَرَ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَٰسِقُونَ
- 24:56 وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَطِيعُوا۟ ٱلرَّسُولَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ
- 24:57 لَا تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مُعْجِزِينَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ وَمَأْوَىٰهُمُ ٱلنَّارُ ۖ وَلَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
- 24:58 يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لِيَسْتَـْٔذِنكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُكُمْ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا۟ ٱلْحُلُمَ مِنكُمْ ثَلَٰثَ مَرَّٰتٍۢ ۚ مِّن قَبْلِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلْفَجْرِ وَحِينَ تَضَعُونَ ثِيَابَكُم مِّنَ ٱلظَّهِيرَةِ وَمِنۢ بَعْدِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلْعِشَآءِ ۚ ثَلَٰثُ عَوْرَٰتٍۢ لَّكُمْ ۚ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَا عَلَيْهِمْ جُنَاحٌۢ بَعْدَهُنَّ ۚ طَوَّٰفُونَ عَلَيْكُم بَعْضُكُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌۭ
- 24:59 وَإِذَا بَلَغَ ٱلْأَطْفَٰلُ مِنكُمُ ٱلْحُلُمَ فَلْيَسْتَـْٔذِنُوا۟ كَمَا ٱسْتَـْٔذَنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌۭ
- 24:60 وَٱلْقَوَٰعِدُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ ٱلَّٰتِى لَا يَرْجُونَ نِكَاحًۭا فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِنَّ جُنَاحٌ أَن يَضَعْنَ ثِيَابَهُنَّ غَيْرَ مُتَبَرِّجَٰتٍۭ بِزِينَةٍۢ ۖ وَأَن يَسْتَعْفِفْنَ خَيْرٌۭ لَّهُنَّ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌۭ

- 24:62 إِنَّمَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَإِذَا كَانُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرٍۢ جَامِعٍۢ لَّمْ يَذْهَبُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يَسْتَـْٔذِنُوهُ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَـْٔذِنُونَكَ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ ۚ فَإِذَا ٱسْتَـْٔذَنُوكَ لِبَعْضِ شَأْنِهِمْ فَأْذَن لِّمَن شِئْتَ مِنْهُمْ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمُ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ

- 24:64 أَلَآ إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ قَدْ يَعْلَمُ مَآ أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ وَيَوْمَ يُرْجَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ فَيُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوا۟ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌۢ

# Dictionary: every branch of every focus root

Every root of the surah's words, each once, headed by the ayah and word where it first occurs; it also serves the later words listed with it.
One entry per branch: a Turkish label and Turkish glosses of its attested senses, then the classical dictionaries' own phrases with their source tags (ayn, sihah, tahdhib, maqayis, mufradat, jamhara). [kalıp] marks a sense the dictionaries attest only inside a fixed expression.
Identity roots come from the quran-data gateway. Word-scoped alternatives are cited analyses of this
exact word. **Echo roots** are observed but withheld mappings: sound-family candidates, not identity.

# s024 Semantic Channel Discovery

## Parent Channels

### 1. [P1 24:1-20] Measure Gives Law a Body
- Semantic invariant: A norm becomes effective by being bounded, placed, counted, witnessed, and finally registered at its proper moral magnitude.
- Surface relation: direct; 24:1-15 anchors the invariant in `سُورَةٌ`, `فَرَضْنَاهَا`, the counted sanctions, the four/fivefold testimony cycles, and the contrast `هَيِّنًا ... عَظِيمٌ`.
- Surprising reach: Lexical branches make legislation spatial and corporeal: a surah resembles an enclosing wall, obligation a scored cut, punishment a measured impact on skin, and culpability an allocated share whose apparent and actual sizes diverge.

#### Subchannel A. Enclosed and Placed Revelation
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A bounded textual unit is delivered, set in its proper rank, incised as a determinate obligation, and made visibly legible.
- Active motifs: enclosing wall `quranic:root_000758:B002/m01`; enclosed or elevated textual segment `quranic:root_000758:B003/m01`; caused delivery `quranic:root_001492:B002/m01`; placement in the fitting station `quranic:root_001492:B004/m01`; scored cut `quranic:root_001144:B001/m01`; obligation fixed to a known limit `quranic:root_001144:B002/m01`; manifest disclosure `quranic:root_000170:B004/m01`; visible sign `quranic:root_000074:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:1 `سُورَةٌ أَنزَلْنَاهَا وَفَرَضْنَاهَا ... آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ`
- Synthesis: The legal opening is not only a descent of propositions. It is an architectural and craft process: a unit is enclosed, lowered into position, scored to a fixed measure, and exposed as a visible sign. The imagery supports the primary reading by giving determinate form to revelation's authority.

#### Subchannel B. Counted Impact on Skin
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Exact quantities terminate in a bodily surface where the sanction is materially received.
- Active motifs: bodily skin or hide `quranic:root_000253:B001/m01`; striking that reaches the skin `quranic:root_000253:B004/m01`; completion to one hundred `quranic:root_001394:B002/m01`; eight as the numerical base of eighty `quranic:root_000206:B002/m01`; numerical oneness `quranic:root_001631:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:2 `كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ ... مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ`; 24:4 `ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً`
- Synthesis: Number and body form one scene rather than two adjacent topics. The count fixes the sanction's extent, while the skin branch identifies its receiving boundary. The latent craft sense of exact completion pressures any reading that would dissolve the stated quantities into an unbounded response.

#### Subchannel C. The Ordinary Witness Threshold
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A charge crosses into adjudicable knowledge only when a fixed number of present observers can articulate it.
- Active motifs: presence with direct observation `quranic:root_000822:B001/m01`; testimony that declares known fact `quranic:root_000822:B002/m01`; the witness as an articulating tongue `quranic:root_000822:B005/m01`; the number four `quranic:root_000536:B001/m01`; bounded individual unit `quranic:root_001631:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:2 `وَلْيَشْهَدْ`; 24:4 `بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَاءَ`; 24:13 `بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَاءَ`
- Synthesis: Presence, knowledge, articulation, and count cooperate as a single evidentiary gate. A claim does not become proof merely by circulation; four embodied positions must convert observation into public declaration.

#### Subchannel D. Reciprocal Oaths as Counterforce
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: When external witnesses are absent, two opposed oath sequences balance accusation and defense through four repetitions and a decisive fifth.
- Active motifs: divine name used in oath `quranic:root_000047:B002/m01`; the number four `quranic:root_000536:B001/m01`; the fifth that completes the series `quranic:root_000439:B001/m01`; mutual imprecation between spouses `quranic:root_001359:B004/m01`; averting a penalty by counter-proof `quranic:root_000466:B001/m01`; wrath surging toward requital `quranic:root_001092:B001/m01`; the self as the sole available witness `quranic:root_001533:B012/m01`; punishment as inflicted pain `quranic:root_000994:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:6 `إِلَّا أَنفُسُهُمْ ... أَرْبَعُ شَهَادَاتٍ بِاللَّهِ`; 24:7 `وَالْخَامِسَةُ ... لَعْنَتَ اللَّهِ`; 24:8 `وَيَدْرَأُ عَنْهَا الْعَذَابَ`; 24:9 `وَالْخَامِسَةَ ... غَضَبَ اللَّهِ`
- Synthesis: The oath procedure is a calibrated counterweight, not a loose appeal to sincerity. Four units establish symmetry; the fifth changes the stakes; the answering sequence actively deflects punishment. Lexical imprecation makes the legal form reciprocal and self-binding.

#### Subchannel E. Mis-Scaled Moral Accounting
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Each participant acquires an individual liability, one actor shoulders its largest share, and speech judged light nearby is registered as great at the decisive station.
- Active motifs: the individual person `quranic:root_001409:B001/m01`; self-acquired gain or liability `quranic:root_001296:B001/m01`; the greatest portion of an affair `quranic:root_001281:B002/m01`; lightness and ease `quranic:root_001608:B002/m01`; magnitude and force `quranic:root_001029:B001/m01`; a grave descending event `quranic:root_001029:B004/m01`; nearness at a place of judgment `quranic:root_001052:B004/m01`; requital of sin `quranic:root_000013:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:11 `لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ ... مَا اكْتَسَبَ ... تَوَلَّى كِبْرَهُ`; 24:15 `تَحْسَبُونَهُ هَيِّنًا وَهُوَ عِندَ اللَّهِ عَظِيمٌ`
- Synthesis: The rumor has an allocation structure: distributed acquisition, a largest share, and a final scale. What feels frictionless in the mouth becomes a weighty event at the adjudicating proximity marked by `عِندَ اللَّهِ`. The channel reframes casual transmission as measurable participation.

### 2. [P1 24:1-20] Speech Moves as a Physical Force
- Semantic invariant: An utterance can be launched, received, relayed, spilled, and intensified; social speech therefore behaves like force moving through material media.
- Surface relation: direct and indirect; 24:4-6 supplies `يَرْمُونَ`, 24:12-16 hearing/tongue/mouth transfer, and 24:14/19 overflow and diffusion.
- Surprising reach: The network materializes accusation as projectile injury and rumor as both fluid overflow and fire propagation, exposing distinct mechanisms rather than one generic “speech” domain.

#### Subchannel A. Accusation as Projectile Injury
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A verbal charge is launched toward a protected target, reaches listeners through abusive sound, and leaves a wound-like mark.
- Active motifs: launching an object `quranic:root_000603:B001/m01`; projectile, point, or struck quarry `quranic:root_000603:B003/m01`; verbal accusation `quranic:root_000603:B008/m01`; inaccurate shot of judgment `quranic:root_000603:B009/m01`; shield or practice target `quranic:root_000466:B005/m01`; abusive speech made audible `quranic:root_000741:B006/m01`; bodily wound `quranic:root_001316:B003/m01`; taking or attacking someone by the tongue `quranic:root_001355:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:4, 24:6 `يَرْمُونَ`; 24:8 `وَيَدْرَأُ عَنْهَا`; 24:15 `بِأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ`; 24:16 `سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ... نَتَكَلَّمَ`
- Synthesis: The charge inherits the mechanics of a shot: projection, target, possible mis-aim, reception, and injury. The protected person is not merely discussed but struck in a social body, while the tongue functions as the attacking instrument and hearing as the point of impact.

#### Subchannel B. Tongue-to-Mouth Relay
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Speech is taken at one bodily interface and immediately reissued from another, producing a relay without a knowledge-bearing pause.
- Active motifs: tongue as speech organ `quranic:root_001355:B001/m01`; tongue as message carrier `quranic:root_001355:B008/m01`; receiving and learning words `quranic:root_001372:B011/m01`; mouth as opening `quranic:root_001190:B001/m01`; opening the mouth in speech `quranic:root_001190:B003/m01`; voiced utterance `quranic:root_001272:B001/m01`; auditory reception `quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:15 `تَلَقَّوْنَهُ بِأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ وَتَقُولُونَ بِأَفْوَاهِكُم`; 24:16 `إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ قُلْتُم`
- Synthesis: The verse's unusual tongue reception becomes a literal transfer mechanism in the branch network. Words are caught, carried, and emitted through organs of speech before knowledge enters the circuit, explaining how repetition can outrun verification.

#### Subchannel C. Discourse as Overflow
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A filled source spills beyond its boundary, and the released material diffuses as circulating talk.
- Active motifs: liquid filling and easy overflow `quranic:root_001192:B001/m01`; expansive immersion in talk `quranic:root_001192:B003/m01`; diffusion among people `quranic:root_000836:B003/m01`; circulating public talk `quranic:root_001272:B007/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:14 `فِيمَا أَفَضْتُمْ فِيهِ`; 24:15-16 `تَقُولُونَ ... قُلْتُم`; 24:19 `أَن تَشِيعَ`
- Synthesis: Overflow and rumor share one process signature: pressure exceeds containment, then material disperses through a population. The hydrological image clarifies that the wrong is not only the proposition's content but the uncontrolled expansion of its carrier medium.

#### Subchannel D. Rumor as a Fire Fed by a Group
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A compact supporting group feeds a fire whose sparks scatter outward, turning collective reinforcement into wider social ignition.
- Active motifs: group gathered around and mutually supporting `quranic:root_001018:B004/m01`; diffusion among people `quranic:root_000836:B003/m01`; feeding and strengthening a fire `quranic:root_000836:B005/m01`; flying sparks `quranic:root_000787:B003/m01`; manifest obscenity that exceeds a boundary `quranic:root_001134:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:11 `عُصْبَةٌ مِنكُمْ`; 24:19 `أَن تَشِيعَ الْفَاحِشَةُ`
- Synthesis: This is not the fluid mechanism of accidental overflow. Here a group supplies fuel and mutual reinforcement, after which sparks distribute the injury. The image usefully pressures the collective's role: proximity and solidarity can become an engine of escalation.

### 3. [P1 24:1-20] Reputation Has an Enclosure, Breach, and Repair
- Semantic invariant: Sexual reputation is treated as an inhabited protected interior whose boundary can be crossed, whose covering can split, and whose integrity can be restored.
- Surface relation: direct and indirect; 24:3-5 and 24:19 anchor chastity, prohibition, transgression, repentance, and repair.
- Surprising reach: Fort, precinct, shell, cover, and wound-relapse senses turn abstract honor into boundary maintenance and make repentance a practical reconstruction rather than a merely verbal reversal.

#### Subchannel A. Fortified Chastity
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Chastity occupies a defended interior protected by fortification, inviolable precinct, and covering.
- Active motifs: preservation inside an encircling fort `quranic:root_000331:B001/m01`; guarded sexual integrity `quranic:root_000331:B002/m01`; inviolable precinct and its protected margin `quranic:root_000313:B003/m01`; protected right or sanctity `quranic:root_000313:B006/m01`; a cover that shields what is beneath it `quranic:root_001096:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:3 `حُرِّمَ`; 24:4 `الْمُحْصَنَاتِ`; 24:5 `غَفُورٌ`
- Synthesis: The protected woman and the protected claim about her become one fortified scene. Chastity is an interior condition, prohibition marks its perimeter, and covering prevents destructive exposure. The spatial model explains why unsupported accusation is treated as boundary violation.

#### Subchannel B. Shell-Break and Exposure
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Obscene speech crosses a fixed perimeter and forces what was enclosed outward, like fruit breaking through its husk.
- Active motifs: exceeding a proper limit `quranic:root_001134:B002/m01`; obscene speech or action `quranic:root_001134:B003/m01`; a ripe date exiting its shell `quranic:root_001156:B002/m01`; false charge that stuns its target or hearer `quranic:root_000157:B002/m01`; the protected sexual interior `quranic:root_000331:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:4 `الْمُحْصَنَاتِ ... الْفَاسِقُونَ`; 24:16 `بُهْتَانٌ عَظِيمٌ`; 24:19 `تَشِيعَ الْفَاحِشَةُ`
- Synthesis: Transgression is rendered as forced emergence through a protective casing. The husk image makes `فسق` a structural exit, while obscene and stunning speech enact the pressure that breaches the enclosure. The result is exposure, not just doctrinal error.

#### Subchannel C. Repair, Reconciliation, and Protective Cover
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: After breach, return is invited, damaged relations are repaired, hostility is removed, and consequence is covered.
- Active motifs: repair opposed to corruption `quranic:root_000876:B001/m01`; reconciliation that removes estrangement `quranic:root_000876:B002/m01`; inviting another to return in repentance `quranic:root_000189:B003/m01`; covering fault and shielding its bearer from consequence `quranic:root_001096:B002/m01`; merciful tenderness `quranic:root_000552:B001/m01`; unowed restorative gift `quranic:root_001163:B003/m01`; declaration of absolution `quranic:root_000666:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:5 `تَابُوا ... وَأَصْلَحُوا ... غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ`; 24:10, 24:14, 24:20 `فَضْلُ اللَّهِ ... وَرَحْمَتُهُ`; 24:16 `سُبْحَانَكَ`
- Synthesis: Repair is multi-step: an offender turns, a relationship is made fit, the fault is covered, and mercy supplies more than bare equilibrium. The absolving force of `سُبْحَانَكَ` also interrupts the rumor by clearing the divine frame of the attributed obscenity.

### 4. [P1 24:1-20] Cognition Can Align or Invert a Report
- Semantic invariant: Before speech becomes public judgment, the mind estimates, orients, and either aligns a report with evidence or turns it away from truth.
- Surface relation: direct; 24:11-19 repeatedly opposes supposition, calculation, inner judgment, manifest falsehood, and divine knowledge.
- Surprising reach: The branches distinguish several epistemic operations concealed by broad labels such as “thinking”: strong inference, weak imagining, accusation, habitual suspicion, internal speech, and directional inversion.

#### Subchannel A. A Gradient from Inference to Suspicion
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A heard report moves through increasingly unstable mental estimates, from inference by a sign to weak imagining, accusation, and habitual mistrust.
- Active motifs: conviction inferred from an indicator `quranic:root_000969:B001/m01`; weak supposition `quranic:root_000969:B003/m01`; accusatory suspicion `quranic:root_000969:B004/m01`; habitual ill opinion of others `quranic:root_000969:B005/m01`; estimating something in the mind `quranic:root_000318:B002/m01`; believing a report so the heart settles `quranic:root_000054:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:11 `لَا تَحْسَبُوهُ شَرًّا`; 24:12 `سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ ... خَيْرًا`; 24:15 `تَحْسَبُونَهُ هَيِّنًا`
- Synthesis: The scene is a decision ladder, not a single state called opinion. The same input may be interpreted through a trustworthy indicator, held as weak conjecture, converted into an accusation, or generalized into a disposition toward others. The commanded good judgment is therefore an active epistemic choice.

#### Subchannel B. Falsehood as Directional Inversion
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A statement is turned off its proper heading, stabilized as a lie, and then used to classify other speakers as liars.
- Active motifs: turning something away from its face or direction `quranic:root_000041:B001/m01`; lie diverted from truth `quranic:root_000041:B002/m01`; judgment weakened and deprived of sound strategy `quranic:root_000041:B006/m01`; falsehood opposed to truth `quranic:root_001290:B001/m01`; assigning falsehood to another `quranic:root_001290:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:11-12 `الْإِفْكِ ... هَذَا إِفْكٌ مُّبِينٌ`; 24:13 `هُمُ الْكَاذِبُونَ`
- Synthesis: `إفك` is not only incorrect content; it is an orientation reversed. Once the report is turned, cognition loses strategic soundness and social actors begin projecting the false classification onto others. The channel makes moral error a directional operation.

#### Subchannel C. Inner Speech Meets Exposed Knowledge
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Unvoiced formulation and inward intention are contrasted with articulated disclosure and knowledge that fully uncovers its object.
- Active motifs: speech formed internally before utterance `quranic:root_001272:B012/m01`; speech as held conviction or doctrine `quranic:root_001272:B013/m01`; mind, intention, and discriminating faculty within the self `quranic:root_001533:B013/m01`; knowledge as the object's disclosure to the knower `quranic:root_001040:B001/m01`; meaning exposed through word or sign `quranic:root_000170:B005/m01`; right-aiming wisdom `quranic:root_000348:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:12 `بِأَنفُسِهِمْ ... وَقَالُوا`; 24:15 `مَا لَيْسَ لَكُم بِهِ عِلْمٌ`; 24:18-19 `يُبَيِّنُ ... عَلِيمٌ ... اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ`
- Synthesis: The decisive boundary lies between what the self formulates, what the mouth releases, and what is actually known. Disclosure is legitimate when it unveils meaning; rumor instead externalizes an inner formulation without the corresponding disclosure of fact.

### 5. [P1 24:1-20] Accusation Pressures Reproductive Continuity
- Semantic invariant: Sexual accusation reaches beyond an isolated act into pairing, marital legitimacy, conception, gestation, birth, and the traces by which lineage becomes socially visible.
- Surface relation: indirect; 24:3-14 supplies marriage, spouses, chastity, self-witness, testimony, mercy, and bodily contact, while the reproductive sequence remains lexically latent.
- Surprising reach: Womb, postpartum blood, afterbirth, birth witness, midwife, and rapid conception branches disclose the lineage stakes that make sexual testimony unusually consequential.

#### Subchannel A. Pairing, Contract, and Sexual Contact
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Two persons are paired through a recognized marital relation whose protected interior includes sexual contact.
- Active motifs: spouse in a marital pair `quranic:root_000652:B002/m01`; joining one thing as the mate of another `quranic:root_000652:B003/m01`; sexual intercourse `quranic:root_001548:B001/m01`; marriage contract `quranic:root_001548:B002/m01`; marriage as a protecting status `quranic:root_000331:B003/m01`; sexual contact `quranic:root_001423:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:3 `يَنكِحُ`; 24:6 `أَزْوَاجَهُمْ`; 24:14 `لَمَسَّكُمْ`; 24:4 `الْمُحْصَنَاتِ`
- Synthesis: Contract, pairing, protected status, and bodily contact form one social-reproductive frame. The latent sexual sense of touch at 24:14 does not replace the surface meaning of affliction; it resonates with the marital field already active and sharpens what an accusation puts at risk.

#### Subchannel B. Gestation and Birth Leave Evidence
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A womb receives conception, carries a child, releases birth material, and is attended by recognizable traces and a receiving agent.
- Active motifs: womb as the child's growing enclosure `quranic:root_000552:B003/m01`; pregnancy and postpartum emergence `quranic:root_001533:B005/m01`; blood or membrane accompanying birth as a witness `quranic:root_000822:B006/m01`; afterbirth and uterine discharge `quranic:root_000994:B009/m01`; midwife receiving the newborn `quranic:root_001198:B007/m01`; rapid conception `quranic:root_001372:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:5, 24:10, 24:14, 24:20 `رَحْمَتُهُ`; 24:6, 24:12 `أَنفُسُهُمْ`; 24:2, 24:4, 24:6, 24:8, 24:13 `شَهَادَة/شُهَدَاء`; 24:2, 24:8, 24:11, 24:14, 24:19 `الْعَذَاب`; 24:4 `تَقْبَلُوا`; 24:15 `تَلَقَّوْنَهُ`
- Synthesis: The branch network assembles a complete reproductive sequence from roots otherwise active in mercy, selfhood, witness, punishment, reception, and verbal relay. This scene usefully reframes why proof rules guard lineage: birth itself yields bodily witnesses, while rumor tries to manufacture social evidence without them.

### 6. [P2 24:21-34] Deviation Leaves a Track
- Semantic invariant: Moral deviation is spatially enacted as a traceable sequence and as distance maintained by a taut, crooked line.
- Surface relation: direct and indirect; 24:21 repeats `تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ`.
- Surprising reach: Footprints, stepwise tracking, a long well-rope, and crooked tension separate the incremental mechanism of following from the deviant condition of the leader followed.

#### Subchannel A. Stepwise Pursuit
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A walker places successive steps; another traces them one by one until the path produces a binding consequence.
- Active motifs: stride and distance between feet `quranic:root_000424:B001/m01`; footprints treated as a path to imitate `quranic:root_000424:B002/m01`; stepping past a boundary `quranic:root_000424:B004/m01`; following an actor or trace `quranic:root_000175:B001/m01`; searching footprint after footprint `quranic:root_000175:B003/m01`; uninterrupted succession `quranic:root_000175:B004/m01`; consequence that follows and remains due `quranic:root_000175:B006/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:21 `لَا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ ... وَمَن يَتَّبِعْ خُطُوَاتِ`
- Synthesis: The warning describes a process with temporal granularity. Each small imitation supplies the location of the next; repeated following becomes continuity, and continuity leaves a liability behind it. The danger lies in the chain, not only its endpoint.

#### Subchannel B. The Long Tether of Rebellion
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A remote, rebellious agent pulls from a distance through a long, tightly twisted line whose crooked heading resists the intended course.
- Active motifs: remoteness and severance `quranic:root_000796:B001/m01`; long tightly twisted rope `quranic:root_000796:B002/m01`; crooked divergence and opposition `quranic:root_000796:B003/m01`; insolent rebel `quranic:root_000796:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:21 `الشَّيْطَانِ` (twice)
- Synthesis: The satanic figure carries a mechanical image distinct from the follower's footsteps. Distance does not remove control: a long tether can transmit pull, and its crooked tension biases every subsequent step. The image materializes remote influence without collapsing it into compulsion.

### 7. [P2 24:21-34] Pardon Removes Residue and Reopens Kinship
- Semantic invariant: Forgiveness clears the material trace of offense, changes bodily orientation toward the offender, and permits provision to flow again through a damaged kin relation.
- Surface relation: direct and indirect; 24:22 joins `يَعْفُوا`, `يَصْفَحُوا`, `يَغْفِرَ`, kinship, capacity, and giving.
- Surprising reach: Wind-erased tracks, a broad face turned away from blame, a joined hand, and protective covering distinguish complementary operations often compressed into a single idea of pardon.

#### Subchannel A. Erasing the Trace
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Punitive pursuit stops, the residual mark is worn away, and the offender is covered against the fault's continuing effect.
- Active motifs: leaving deserved punishment `quranic:root_001032:B001/m01`; wind or time erasing a track `quranic:root_001032:B006/m01`; protective covering `quranic:root_001096:B001/m01`; covering fault and shielding its bearer `quranic:root_001096:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:22 `وَلْيَعْفُوا ... أَن يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ... غَفُورٌ`
- Synthesis: Pardon first changes the offense's persistence. The pursuer releases punishment, then the trace by which the offense remains socially retraceable is erased, and protective covering prevents continued exposure. These are successive operations, not synonyms.

#### Subchannel B. Turning the Broad Side Away
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A person withdraws the accusing face from the fault and converts confrontation into an open-handed social closure.
- Active motifs: broad face or side `quranic:root_000867:B001/m01`; graceful turning away from fault `quranic:root_000867:B002/m01`; joining palm to palm `quranic:root_000867:B004/m01`; the rejected alternative of turning away a petitioner `quranic:root_000867:B009/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:22 `وَلْيَصْفَحُوا`
- Synthesis: The face branch gives pardon a bodily orientation: one ceases presenting the fault as the object of confrontation. The hand-contact branch extends that turn into renewed social contact, while refusal of a petitioner remains the live contrary outcome in the verse's gift context.

#### Subchannel C. Provision Re-enters the Kin Network
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Material capacity is redirected toward a near relative after estrangement, restoring both support and relational proximity.
- Active motifs: blood kinship `quranic:root_001212:B003/m01`; kinship as a womb-derived bond `quranic:root_000552:B002/m01`; capacity beyond immediate need `quranic:root_001163:B001/m01`; unowed gift `quranic:root_001163:B003/m01`; giving or bringing a grant `quranic:root_000009:B002/m01`; nearness opposed to distance `quranic:root_001212:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:22 `أُولُو الْفَضْلِ وَالسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤْتُوا أُولِي الْقُرْبَى`
- Synthesis: The social repair becomes complete only when resources move again. Proximity is not sentimental: the kin bond creates a route, capacity supplies the material, and giving reopens a connection that resentment had threatened to close.

### 8. [P2 24:21-34] Speech Becomes Bodily and Moral Evidence
- Semantic invariant: Accusatory speech returns through bodies, is sorted by moral quality, and terminates in exoneration or allocated consequence.
- Surface relation: direct and indirect; 24:23-26 proceeds from accusation of protected women to bodily testimony, truth disclosed, qualitative pairing, exoneration, forgiveness, and honorable provision.
- Surprising reach: Tongues, hands, and feet turn discourse into embodied evidence, while purity and corruption branches classify not only persons but words, deeds, and the company that sustains them.

#### Subchannel A. Speaking Limbs Return the Charge
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A verbal projectile aimed at a protected person is answered when the accuser's own organs become witnesses to deliberate action.
- Active motifs: verbal accusation `quranic:root_000603:B008/m01`; guarded chastity `quranic:root_000331:B002/m01`; testimony that declares known fact `quranic:root_000822:B002/m01`; tongue as speaking organ `quranic:root_001355:B001/m01`; hand as bodily instrument `quranic:root_001693:B001/m01`; foot or leg `quranic:root_000546:B001/m01`; intended deed `quranic:root_001046:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:23 `يَرْمُونَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ`; 24:24 `تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَلْسِنَتُهُمْ وَأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُم بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ`
- Synthesis: The accusation reverses direction. Organs formerly used to transmit or enact it cease being private instruments and become public declarants. The body closes the evidentiary gap that rumor attempted to exploit.

#### Subchannel B. Words and Persons Are Sorted by Quality
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Bad speech, bad action, and corrupt companionship collect on one side; wholesome persons and expressions collect on the other.
- Active motifs: intrinsic vileness extending to false words and ugly deeds `quranic:root_000386:B001/m01`; corruption reinforced by corrupt companions `quranic:root_000386:B003/m01`; wholesomeness opposed to corruption `quranic:root_000961:B001/m01`; purification from contaminating matter `quranic:root_000961:B003/m01`; falsely attributing unsaid words `quranic:root_001272:B005/m01`; circulating public talk `quranic:root_001272:B007/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:26 `الْخَبِيثَاتُ لِلْخَبِيثِينَ ... وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ لِلطَّيِّبِينَ ... مِمَّا يَقُولُونَ`
- Synthesis: The pairing is a sorting operation whose inputs include utterances, actions, associates, and persons. It does not merely label two static classes; it shows how speech finds a sustaining moral environment and how purification separates a person from contaminating attribution.

#### Subchannel C. Exoneration Opens Honorable Provision
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Separation from a false attribution is followed by protective covering and an apportioned, honorable gift.
- Active motifs: exonerating separation from person, deed, or defect `quranic:root_000099:B002/m01`; covering fault and consequence `quranic:root_001096:B002/m01`; apportioned provision `quranic:root_000560:B001/m01`; nourishing provision `quranic:root_000560:B002/m01`; intrinsic honor and generosity `quranic:root_001294:B001/m01`; what is precious to its holder `quranic:root_001294:B010/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:26 `مُبَرَّءُونَ ... لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ`
- Synthesis: Exoneration is a release operation, after which covering prevents the lie's residue from adhering. Provision then restores both material share and social honor. The outcome is not simply innocence but a renewed allocation.

### 9. [P2 24:21-34] Apertures Govern Access
- Semantic invariant: Houses, eyes, bodily openings, and garments are apertures whose ethical function depends on controlled entry, attenuation, guarding, and closure.
- Surface relation: direct; 24:27-31 moves from house entry and permission to lowered sight, guarded openings, displayed adornment, covering, and the garment opening.
- Surprising reach: Doorway protocol and bodily modesty become structurally homologous without being collapsed: each has an exterior, an interior, an aperture, an authorized user, and a reversible access operation.

#### Subchannel A. Threshold Recognition, Permission, and Reversal
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A visitor reaches an inhabited boundary, establishes recognition, receives or lacks authorization, and reverses course when refused.
- Active motifs: house as dwelling `quranic:root_000166:B001/m01`; entry into an interior `quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`; inward secret or hidden side `quranic:root_000464:B003/m01`; authorization from a gatekeeper `quranic:root_000022:B004/m01`; detecting another by sight, hearing, or felt presence `quranic:root_000059:B002/m01`; inhabitants joined by dwelling `quranic:root_000064:B001/m01`; return to the point of origin `quranic:root_000544:B001/m01`; a spoken answer sent back `quranic:root_000544:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:27 `لَا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتًا ... حَتَّى تَسْتَأْنِسُوا ... عَلَى أَهْلِهَا`; 24:28 `حَتَّى يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ ... ارْجِعُوا فَارْجِعُوا`; 24:29 `بُيُوتًا غَيْرَ مَسْكُونَةٍ`
- Synthesis: Entry is a reversible protocol, not a one-way physical motion. Recognition tests whether an interior is socially available; permission opens it; refusal returns both message and visitor. The hidden-interior branch clarifies what the threshold protects.

#### Subchannel B. Gaze as an Attenuated Valve
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Visual intake is deliberately reduced while vigilance maintains the boundary against accidental overreach.
- Active motifs: ocular seeing `quranic:root_000121:B001/m01`; lowering or diminishing a faculty `quranic:root_001093:B001/m01`; guarding and sustained care `quranic:root_000342:B001/m01`; alert self-restraint against slips `quranic:root_000342:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:30-31 `يَغُضُّوا/يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ/أَبْصَارِهِنَّ وَيَحْفَظُوا/يَحْفَظْنَ`
- Synthesis: Lowering the gaze is a controlled reduction, like restricting flow through an opening; it is not the abolition of sight. Guarding supplies the sustained attention required to keep that reduction stable in changing encounters.

#### Subchannel C. The Body as a Vulnerable Opening
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A bodily opening resembles a gap in a wall or exposed frontier that requires inspection and defense.

- Ayah anchors: 24:30-31 `وَيَحْفَظُوا/يَحْفَظْنَ فُرُوجَهُمْ/فُرُوجَهُنَّ`; 24:31 `عَوْرَاتِ النِّسَاءِ`
- Synthesis: The sexual sense remains primary, but the lexical field gives it defensive geometry. An opening can be structurally necessary and still vulnerable; guarding is therefore maintenance of a frontier, not denial that the aperture exists.

#### Subchannel D. Garment Closure Over the Opening

- Ayah anchors: 24:31 `لَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ ... وَلْيَضْرِبْنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَى جُيُوبِهِنَّ`
- Synthesis: The scene is a precise closure operation: a covering is redirected onto an existing opening, changing the path by which adornment becomes visible. It complements bodily guarding but remains a distinct garment mechanism.

### 10. [P2 24:21-34] Visibility Rights Follow Social Roles
- Semantic invariant: Proximity does not authorize visibility by physical nearness alone; named kinship, marital, dependency, age, and desire roles determine the access relation.
- Surface relation: direct; 24:31 enumerates husbands, ascendants, descendants, siblings, women, dependents, followers without sexual need, and children below awareness.
- Surprising reach: The branches expose role mechanics inside the list: marital play and mutual accommodation, parental formation, dependent ownership, felt need, and the dangerous counter-image of a follower who pursues women.

#### Subchannel A. Marital and Kin Roles
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A household graph links spouses, parents, siblings, and descendants through distinct forms of formation, nurture, intimacy, and lineage.
- Active motifs: husband in a marital relation `quranic:root_000134:B001/m01`; intimate marital companionship `quranic:root_000134:B005/m01`; fatherhood as generation and nurture `quranic:root_000007:B001/m01`; sibling kinship `quranic:root_000020:B001/m01`; filiation and descent `quranic:root_000156:B007/m01`; women as a social class `quranic:root_001500:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:31 `لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ آبَائِهِنَّ ... أَوْ أَبْنَائِهِنَّ ... أَوْ إِخْوَانِهِنَّ ... أَوْ نِسَائِهِنَّ`
- Synthesis: The permissions are indexed to differentiated relations, not an undifferentiated category of familiarity. Each role carries a distinct social history—generation, descent, siblinghood, or marital intimacy—that makes proximity intelligible.

#### Subchannel B. Dependence, Need, and Childhood
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Access narrows or widens according to dependency and whether sexual need or perceptual maturity is active.
- Active motifs: child at an early life stage `quranic:root_000942:B001/m01`; child-bearing companionship and care `quranic:root_000942:B002/m01`; urgent need including sexual need `quranic:root_000024:B001/m01`; owned dependent under another's disposal `quranic:root_001444:B002/m01`; ordinary following or service `quranic:root_000175:B001/m01`; the contrary follower who pursues women `quranic:root_000175:B011/m01`; adult man as a sexed role `quranic:root_000546:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:31 `مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُنَّ أَوِ التَّابِعِينَ غَيْرِ أُولِي الْإِرْبَةِ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ أَوِ الطِّفْلِ`
- Synthesis: The list is a functional risk map. Dependency alone does not settle the relation; need, pursuit, sexed role, and childhood awareness alter how a follower participates in the scene. The contrary branch of “following women” sharpens why lack of `إربة` matters.

### 11. [P2 24:21-34] Marriage Converts Lack into Household Capacity
- Semantic invariant: Marriage is a transition from unpaired status toward a protected household, mediated by resources, sufficiency, and restraint during delay.
- Surface relation: direct; 24:32-33 joins the unpaired, arranged marriage, poverty, divine enrichment, inability to find marriage, and chastity.
- Surprising reach: Sufficiency branches explicitly treat marriage itself as enrichment and fortification, while patient delay appears as a controlled temporal operation rather than passive exclusion.

#### Subchannel A. From Unpaired Status to Contracted Pair
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A person lacking a spouse is actively brought into a recognized marital bond.
- Active motifs: interruption of spousal pairing `quranic:root_000073:B001/m01`; causing another to enter marriage `quranic:root_001548:B003/m01`; marriage contract `quranic:root_001548:B002/m01`; acquisition of marital affiliation `quranic:root_001548:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:32 `وَأَنكِحُوا الْأَيَامَى مِنكُمْ`; 24:33 `لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا`
- Synthesis: The unpaired state is not treated as an essence. A communal causative act and a legal bond convert it into affiliation. The operation distributes responsibility beyond the prospective spouses alone.

#### Subchannel B. Poverty Becomes Sufficiency
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Material need is met by an enlarging gift that makes a household viable, with marriage itself functioning as a form of sufficiency.
- Active motifs: material poverty and need `quranic:root_001169:B002/m01`; material independence `quranic:root_001110:B001/m01`; functional sufficiency `quranic:root_001110:B002/m01`; marriage as enrichment and protection `quranic:root_001110:B006/m01`; breadth of means `quranic:root_001647:B003/m01`; unowed divine gift `quranic:root_001163:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:32 `إِن يَكُونُوا فُقَرَاءَ يُغْنِهِمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ`; 24:33 `حَتَّى يُغْنِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ`
- Synthesis: Enrichment is not reducible to cash accumulation. It includes enough function, widened capacity, and the stabilizing relation created by marriage. The sequence reframes economic lack as a condition that can be transformed rather than a permanent bar.

#### Subchannel C. Restrained Waiting
- Reading type: mixed

- Synthesis: Waiting is an active containment scene with a specified terminus, not indefinite suspension. Restraint protects the sexual boundary while gradual easing and recognized good prepare a changed material state.

### 12. [P2 24:21-34] Dependent Status Can Be Written Toward Release or Forced Toward Exploitation
- Semantic invariant: Power over dependents takes opposite procedural forms: a written, funded route out of ownership or coercive conversion of another's body into worldly return.
- Surface relation: direct and indirect; 24:33 places emancipation contract, owned status, monetary grant, coercion, prostitution, chastity, and worldly goods in one contested field.
- Surprising reach: Writing branches assemble, inscribe, bind, and finally emancipate; coercion branches instead override aversion and turn sexual violation into an extractive transaction.

#### Subchannel A. The Emancipation Contract
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Separated terms are joined into writing, made binding, and directed toward release from owned status.
- Active motifs: joining parts into one construction `quranic:root_001283:B001/m01`; inscribed document `quranic:root_001283:B002/m01`; binding legal determination `quranic:root_001283:B003/m01`; manumission contract for staged payment `quranic:root_001283:B005/m01`; owned human status `quranic:root_001444:B002/m01`; enslaved person opposed to the free `quranic:root_000973:B001/m01`; enslaved youth or servant `quranic:root_001130:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:32 `عِبَادِكُمْ وَإِمَائِكُمْ`; 24:33 `يَبْتَغُونَ الْكِتَابَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ`
- Synthesis: The four writing senses form a procedural sequence: assemble terms, record them, give them binding force, and orient performance toward freedom. The contract is therefore a machine for changing status, not merely a document about it.

#### Subchannel B. Capital Transfers Capacity
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The party holding resources transfers part of that capacity so the dependent can perform the release agreement.
- Active motifs: accumulated property `quranic:root_001457:B001/m01`; giving and delivery `quranic:root_000009:B002/m01`; unowed material gift `quranic:root_001163:B003/m01`; generosity as a gift-bearing quality `quranic:root_000452:B005/m01`; beneficial good recognized in another `quranic:root_000452:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:33 `إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا وَآتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي آتَاكُمْ`
- Synthesis: Contract alone cannot alter status if all capacity remains with the owner. Granting money redistributes the means of performance and makes the written route materially traversable. The verse locates the owner's capital inside a prior chain of giving.

#### Subchannel C. Coerced Sexual Extraction
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A controller overrides another's aversion, presses her toward prostitution, and seeks a worldly return from the forced act.

- Synthesis: This is the inverse of funded release. The controlling party extracts value by defeating another's will and protective boundary. Keeping aversion, coercion, sexual transgression, and worldly return distinct reveals the full transaction rather than hiding it inside a broad category of immorality.

### 13. [P2 24:21-34] Revelation Projects Precedent into the Present
- Semantic invariant: Instruction is delivered and made manifest by setting a prior case before present hearers as a visible, affective guide.
- Surface relation: direct; 24:34 joins descending signs, clarification, example, predecessors, and admonition.

#### Subchannel B. Prior Case as Affective Warning

### 21. [P4 24:47-64] Judgment Exposes Direction

- Synthesis: The scene measures orientation by motion after speech. Profession points one way, but a separated portion physically and socially reverses. The flock-like sense of `فريق` sharpens how withdrawal breaks a unit away from its declared course.

- Ayah anchors: 24:48 `دُعُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ`; 24:49 `وَإِن يَكُن لَّهُمُ الْحَقُّ يَأْتُوا إِلَيْهِ مُذْعِنِينَ`

### 22. [P4 24:47-64] Enacted Obedience Outweighs Maximal Oath
- Semantic invariant: Verbal intensity cannot substitute for ordinary, recognizable compliance whose reality is disclosed by conduct.
- Surface relation: direct; 24:53 contrasts strenuous oaths with `طَاعَةٌ مَّعْرُوفَةٌ` and divine knowledge of action.
- Surprising reach: Oath, exertion, command, recognized good, inward expertise, and deliberate work form two rival proof systems: amplified assertion and observable performance.

#### Subchannel A. The Oath Stack Amplifies Assertion
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Speakers bind a divine-name oath, intensify it with their utmost effort, and promise immediate execution if commanded.
- Active motifs: sworn division of liability `quranic:root_001226:B004/m01`; oath made by the right hand `quranic:root_001698:B003/m01`; divine name in oath `quranic:root_000047:B002/m01`; exerting full capacity under strain `quranic:root_000268:B001/m01`; binding command `quranic:root_000051:B002/m01`; speech brought into utterance `quranic:root_001272:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:53 `وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ لَئِنْ أَمَرْتَهُمْ لَيَخْرُجُنَّ`
- Synthesis: Each lexical component raises verbal force: sacred name, formal oath, bodily side, maximum effort, and promised response. The stack is impressive precisely so the counter-demand can reject assertion as the governing evidence.

#### Subchannel B. Recognizable Conduct Supplies Proof
- Reading type: mixed

- Ayah anchors: 24:53 `لَا تُقْسِمُوا طَاعَةٌ مَّعْرُوفَةٌ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ`
- Synthesis: Known obedience is visible by its trace and norm-governed form. Deliberate work supplies the evidence that speech sought to provide, while expertise reaches the action's inward quality. The scene replaces oath volume with performative recognizability.

### 24. [P4 24:47-64] The Messenger Is a Bounded Carrier

- Ayah anchors: 24:61 `أَن تَأْكُلُوا جَمِيعًا أَوْ أَشْتَاتًا`
- Synthesis: Gathering and scattering describe configurations, not grades of legitimacy. A shared vessel can gather bodies into one scene, but permission persists when they disperse. Social inclusion is therefore not made dependent on a single seating form.

#### Subchannel E. Greeting Makes Entry Safe and Wholesome
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: On crossing a household threshold, entrants address the social self with a greeting that restores safety and carries stable good.
- Active motifs: entry into an interior `quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`; safety and freedom from defect `quranic:root_000737:B001/m01`; the self as the same social body `quranic:root_001533:B012/m01`; greeting that invokes life and peace `quranic:root_000383:B007/m01`; stable increasing good `quranic:root_000109:B004/m01`; wholesomeness opposed to corruption `quranic:root_000961:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:61 `فَإِذَا دَخَلْتُم بُيُوتًا فَسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَنفُسِكُمْ تَحِيَّةً مِّنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ مُبَارَكَةً طَيِّبَةً`
- Synthesis: Entry changes physical location; greeting repairs the social boundary crossed. Addressing others as `أنفسكم` identifies host and entrant as parts of one body, while safety, blessing, and wholesomeness specify the state the greeting is meant to create.

### 27. [P4 24:47-64] Collective Work Requires Visible Permission
- Semantic invariant: A common undertaking remains coherent when gathering, attendance, personal departure, and warning are handled through explicit authorization rather than hidden extraction.
- Surface relation: direct and indirect; 24:62-63 joins a gathering affair, permission for personal concerns, the messenger's call, stealth exit behind others, opposition to command, trial, and painful impact.
- Surprising reach: Resolve gathered from scattered opinion, assembly space, sword-like extraction, concealment behind another body, and metallurgical testing make attendance a problem of visible cohesion.

#### Subchannel A. A Gathered Affair and an Authorized Exception
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Participants collect around a resolved common matter; one person's separate concern can be accommodated through explicit permission.
- Active motifs: resolution that gathers scattered judgment `quranic:root_000259:B003/m01`; place or call that gathers people `quranic:root_000259:B004/m01`; significant common affair `quranic:root_000773:B001/m01`; individual purpose sought `quranic:root_000773:B002/m01`; affair or matter as the shared object `quranic:root_000051:B001/m01`; authorization to leave `quranic:root_000022:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:62 `عَلَى أَمْرٍ جَامِعٍ لَّمْ يَذْهَبُوا حَتَّى يَسْتَأْذِنُوهُ ... لِبَعْضِ شَأْنِهِمْ فَأْذَن لِّمَن شِئْتَ`
- Synthesis: The group is held together by more than co-presence: dispersed judgments have been collected into an undertaking. Permission makes a personal exception visible and bounded, allowing the common affair to remain coherent while acknowledging a distinct concern.

#### Subchannel B. Stealth Exit as Extraction
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A participant draws himself out of the assembly gradually and hides the movement behind another person's body.
- Active motifs: drawing an object out gently and invisibly `quranic:root_000736:B001/m01`; secret removal resembling theft `quranic:root_000736:B002/m01`; slipping out through a crowd `quranic:root_000736:B004/m01`; taking refuge behind another `quranic:root_001385:B001/m01`; mutual concealment and one-by-one withdrawal `quranic:root_001385:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:63 `الَّذِينَ يَتَسَلَّلُونَ مِنكُمْ لِوَاذًا`
- Synthesis: Unauthorized absence is rendered as an extraction process, not a simple change of location. Gradual motion reduces visibility, crowd density provides cover, and another body becomes a shield. The mechanism is the negative image of explicit permission.

#### Subchannel C. Opposition Triggers Trial or Painful Impact
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Divergence from the governing command exposes the dissenter to testing that may arrive as social disruption or bodily pain.
- Active motifs: taking a route contrary to another's `quranic:root_000433:B004/m01`; vigilant avoidance of danger `quranic:root_000301:B001/m01`; assay that separates sound from unsound `quranic:root_001128:B001/m01`; ordeal and affliction `quranic:root_001128:B004/m01`; calamity striking a person `quranic:root_000889:B004/m01`; inflicted pain `quranic:root_000046:B002/m01`; punishment as severe hurt `quranic:root_000994:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:63 `فَلْيَحْذَرِ الَّذِينَ يُخَالِفُونَ عَنْ أَمْرِهِ أَن تُصِيبَهُمْ فِتْنَةٌ أَوْ يُصِيبَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ`
- Synthesis: Opposition is directional divergence, and warning asks the dissenter to recognize the exposed path that follows. Trial tests composition; calamity and painful punishment describe possible outcomes. The branches keep diagnostic testing distinct from inflicted consequence.

#### Subchannel D. The Messenger's Call Is Not an Ordinary Summons
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A call carried by the messenger establishes a relation unlike reciprocal peer-calling and therefore cannot be treated as casual background sound.
- Active motifs: summons by voice `quranic:root_000478:B001/m01`; messenger and message-bearing role `quranic:root_000563:B002/m01`; parts or persons set in reciprocal relation `quranic:root_000133:B001/m01`; disclosed knowledge of hidden conduct `quranic:root_001040:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:63 `لَا تَجْعَلُوا دُعَاءَ الرَّسُولِ بَيْنَكُمْ كَدُعَاءِ بَعْضِكُم بَعْضًا قَدْ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ`
- Synthesis: Peer calls circulate laterally among comparable parts; the messenger's call carries an assigned office and payload. Treating the two alike erases the relation that makes collective authorization binding, even if stealth temporarily hides the response from other participants.

### 28. [P4 24:47-64] No Path Leaves the Owner's Reach
- Semantic invariant: Distributed human control remains inside encompassing possession and knowledge, so attempted escape ends in return, report, and a destination with no external refuge.
- Surface relation: direct and indirect; 24:57 denies escape and names fire as refuge and destination, while 24:64 encloses heavens and earth within divine possession, return, report, and knowledge.
- Surprising reach: Owned dependents and keys earlier in P4 activate latent sovereignty branches; open-earth flight, failed outrunning, desert ambiguity, shelter, fire, and return turn final accountability into a closed trajectory.

#### Subchannel A. Local Control Sits Inside Encompassing Possession
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Human ownership and delegated control are nested inside sovereignty that encompasses the upper and lower world and knows every state within it.
- Active motifs: political and divine sovereignty `quranic:root_001444:B003/m01`; owned property and delegated disposal `quranic:root_001444:B002/m02`; sky and all that rises overhead `quranic:root_000745:B004/m01`; earth as the lower field `quranic:root_000025:B001/m01`; complete inclusion of parts `quranic:root_001315:B003/m02`; knowledge that uncovers its object `quranic:root_001040:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:58 `مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ`; 24:61 `مَا مَلَكْتُم مَّفَاتِحَهُ`; 24:64 `لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ... وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ`
- Synthesis: Human control is real but nested. The same ownership root that marks dependents and keys opens onto sovereignty, while sky, earth, totality, and knowledge close the containing frame. No local possessor controls an outside.

#### Subchannel B. Return Ends in Report
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Agents are sent back to the originating authority, their deliberate acts are converted into report, and their actual condition becomes fully known.
- Active motifs: return to an original source `quranic:root_000544:B001/m01`; reported news carrying consequential knowledge `quranic:root_001464:B002/m01`; deliberate deed `quranic:root_001046:B001/m01`; bounded day of occurrence `quranic:root_001700:B001/m01`; knowledge as complete disclosure `quranic:root_001040:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:64 `وَيَوْمَ يُرْجَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ فَيُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوا وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ`
- Synthesis: Return is not spatial closure alone. Action is translated into informative report, and the subject hears the disclosed meaning of what was done. The process joins trajectory, event-time, deed, and knowledge in one endpoint.

#### Subchannel C. Failed Escape Finds Fire as Refuge
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Fugitives try to outrun reach across open earth, fail to produce an outside, and arrive at a shelter that is itself burning destination.
- Active motifs: incapacity to accomplish an act `quranic:root_000985:B001/m01`; escaping or outrunning pursuit `quranic:root_000985:B002/m01`; lower open earth `quranic:root_000025:B001/m01`; joining a place that receives and shelters `quranic:root_000070:B001/m01`; burning fire `quranic:root_001564:B002/m01`; endpoint and final outcome `quranic:root_000897:B001/m01`; desert poised between deliverance and destruction `quranic:root_001186:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:52 `الْفَائِزُونَ`; 24:57 `لَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مُعْجِزِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَأْوَاهُمُ النَّارُ وَلَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ`
- Synthesis: The escape scene inverts the success sense active at 24:52. Open terrain appears to offer outrunning, but no external refuge exists; the receiving shelter is fire, and the traveled route terminates there. The desert branch preserves the sharp lexical boundary between deliverance and destruction.

## Cross-Pericope Channels

### X1. Assertion Becomes Credible Through Embodied Proof
- Semantic invariant: A claim cannot authorize itself; credibility emerges when assertion passes through a bounded evidentiary procedure and becomes answerable to bodies or observable conduct.
- Pericopes: P1 24:1-20, P2 24:21-34, and P4 24:47-64.
- Bridge: role progression and contrast. P1 establishes counted witness testimony and a calibrated oath substitute; P2 reverses the accusing body into a witness; P4 contrasts intensified oath speech with recognizable action.
- Canonical placements: P1 Parent 1, Subchannels C-D; P2 Parent 8, Subchannel A; P4 Parent 22, Subchannels A-B.
- Ayah arc: 24:4-10 and 24:13; 24:23-25; 24:47-54.
- Synthesis: The evidentiary role moves progressively outward. Direct observers first convert knowledge into testimony, and the exceptional oath procedure binds speakers through a balanced form when observers are unavailable. The body then supplies testimony about its own deeds, while the later obedience scene makes conduct, not oath volume, the decisive disclosure. The bridge preserves the difference between a legally calibrated oath and an oath used to postpone performance.

### X2. Protected Interiors Require Controlled Permeability
- Semantic invariant: An interior remains protective and productive when its boundary selects what may enter, leave, or become visible rather than functioning as either total exposure or total closure.
- Pericopes: P1 24:1-20, P2 24:21-34, P3 24:35-46, and P4 24:47-64.
- Bridge: repeated scene signature with role progression. A defended interior is breached and repaired in P1; house, gaze, body, and garment apertures receive explicit operators in P2; fitted enclosure contains while transmitting light in P3; timed, life-stage, and greeting protocols regulate household permeability in P4.
- Canonical placements: P1 Parent 3, Subchannels A-C; P2 Parent 9, Subchannels A-D; P3 Parent 14, Subchannel A; P4 Parent 25, Subchannels A-D, and Parent 26, Subchannel E.
- Ayah arc: 24:3-5 and 24:19; 24:27-31; 24:35; 24:58-61.
- Synthesis: The shared scene contains an interior, a boundary, something that may cross it, and an operation that governs the crossing. P1 identifies the protected interest and the damage of breach. P2 differentiates recognition, permission, attenuation, guarding, and garment closure. The lamp apparatus shows that enclosure can concentrate and transmit a good without surrendering containment. P4 then makes access responsive to time and maturity and uses greeting to restore safety after entry. The whole-surah invariant is controlled transmission through a maintained boundary.

### X3. Orientation Becomes Track, Route, Choice, and Destination
- Semantic invariant: Moral and epistemic orientation becomes legible by generating a trace, entering a route, producing approach or withdrawal, and terminating at an accountable destination.
- Pericopes: P1 24:1-20, P2 24:21-34, P3 24:35-46, and P4 24:47-64.
- Bridge: causal sequence and role progression. P1 turns falsehood into a reversed heading; P2 converts heading into followed steps and transmitted pull; P3 supplies landmark and straight route; P4 exposes orientation through movement toward or away from judgment and closes the trajectory in return and report.
- Canonical placements: P1 Parent 4, Subchannel B; P2 Parent 6, Subchannels A-B; P3 Parent 20, Subchannels A-B; P4 Parent 21, Subchannels A-B and D, and Parent 28, Subchannels B-C.
- Ayah arc: 24:11-13; 24:21; 24:35 and 24:44-46; 24:47-52, 24:57, and 24:64.
- Synthesis: A report first acquires a heading in cognition. Repeated imitation extends that heading into a path, while remote crooked pull explains how deviation can persist across distance. Light and manifest signs then make an alternative course visible and traversable. At judgment, voiced orientation is tested by actual approach, withdrawal, or obedient movement. Return, report, and final refuge supply the endpoint, so direction is never merely metaphorical position; it is a course whose successive acts arrive somewhere.

### X4. Bounded Delivery Reverses Uncontrolled Relay
- Semantic invariant: Responsible transmission joins source, payload, placement, clarification, carrier limit, and receiver liability; circulation without those boundaries multiplies speech while severing it from knowledge.
- Pericopes: P1 24:1-20, P2 24:21-34, and P4 24:47-64.
- Bridge: contrast and reversal with carrier-role progression. P1 stages horizontal tongue-to-mouth relay, overflow, and group-fed diffusion; P2 stages descending instruction placed and clarified for present hearers; P4 bounds the messenger's load, terminus, pace, and authority while assigning response to the audience.
- Canonical placements: P1 Parent 2, Subchannels B-D; P2 Parent 13, Subchannels A-B; P4 Parent 24, Subchannels A-B, and Parent 27, Subchannel D.
- Ayah arc: 24:11-19; 24:34; 24:54 and 24:63.
- Synthesis: Both rumor and instruction move through a social field, but movement alone does not make them equivalent. Rumor is received and reissued before a knowledge-bearing pause, then expands through overflow and reinforcement. Revelation arrives from a named source, is placed, made visible, and clarified. The messenger carries that payload only to its assigned boundary, and the audience retains the burden of response. The later distinction between the messenger's call and peer-calling completes the reversal from uncontrolled circulation to accountable conveyance.

## Additional Standalone Subchannels

### S9. [P2 24:21-34] Bast Fiber Becomes Dense Cloth
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Bast fiber is cleaned into usable strands, spun under stable rotation, woven and twisted, and compacted into strong cloth.
- Active motifs: bast fiber prepared as strands for twisting `quranic:root_001355:B009/m01`; spindle rotated until the twist and whorl hold firm `quranic:root_000469:B007/m01`; skilled weaving, spinning, and twisting `quranic:root_000217:B007/m01`; cloth strengthened by abundant dense yarn `quranic:root_000043:B012/m01`; tightly secured weave `quranic:root_000347:B010/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:15, 24:24 forms of `أَلْسِنَة`; 24:25, 24:49 forms of `حَقّ`; 24:35 `دُرِّيٌّ`; 24:43 `جِبَالٍ`; 24:61 forms of `تَأْكُلُوا`
- Synthesis: Preparation, rotation, twist, interlacing, and density form one manufacture sequence. The scene materializes the veil and garment operations of 24:31 as a made boundary whose protective strength depends on many aligned strands, reframing modest covering as maintained material structure rather than an undifferentiated surface.

### S10. [P3 24:35-46] Water Tests and Seals a Stitched Skin
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Two hide panels are stitched into a waterskin, water is introduced to swell the stitch holes, leaks expose defects, and a sound seam closes around the retained liquid.
- Active motifs: stitching the two sides and upper seam of a waterskin `quranic:root_000438:B011/m01`; water leaking and dripping through stitch holes `quranic:root_000691:B003/m01`; filling the skin so stitch holes swell shut and defects become visible `quranic:root_000691:B004/m01`; closed stitching that retains water `quranic:root_001284:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:29 `تَكْتُمُونَ`; 24:31 `بِخُمُرِهِنَّ`; 24:39 `كَسَرَابٍ`
- Synthesis: Water is both cargo and test medium: contact pressurizes the new vessel, reveals faulty joins, and helps a sound seam close. This supports the mirage contrast at 24:39 by giving real water consequences that an optical substitute cannot produce. A mirage cannot swell a seam, disclose a leak, or remain available inside a container.

### S11. [P2 24:21-34] Cleaving Soil Begins a Delayed Harvest
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A cultivator splits the ground, places and covers grain, irrigates the field, waits for ears to emerge, and carries the cut crop to the threshing floor.
- Active motifs: cereal grain and seed `quranic:root_000286:B001/m01`; farmer cleaving soil for planting `quranic:root_001175:B003/m01`; burying seed beneath earth `quranic:root_001307:B008/m01`; irrigating land and crop with lifted water `quranic:root_000751:B001/m01`; grain putting forth an ear `quranic:root_000672:B008/m01`; carrying harvested crop to the threshing floor `quranic:root_000582:B006/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:19, 24:22 forms of `حَبَّ`; 24:22 `سَبِيلِ`; 24:31, 24:51 forms of `فَلَحَ`; 24:36 `تُرْفَعَ`; 24:39, 24:55, 24:57 forms of `كَفَرَ`; 24:43 `سَنَا`
- Synthesis: The agricultural sense of `فلاح` expands the success named at 24:31 into a causal sequence. Flourishing begins with an opening cut, passes through hidden seed and sustained watering, and becomes visible only in ear and harvest. The scene also materializes the provision of 24:38 as an outcome prepared through ordered work rather than an immediate possession.

### S13. [P3 24:35-46] A House Rises from Foundation, Mud Brick, and Timber

### S14. [P4 24:47-64] Repeated Visits Carry a Patient toward Recovery
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Illness produces pain, attendants care for the patient, visitors return repeatedly, and the patient's condition moves through convalescence into recovery.

- Synthesis: The sick person named in 24:61 activates a social process, not only an exemption. ### S15. [P3 24:35-46] A Camel Auction Escalates the Market
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A camel is displayed for sale, prospective buyers raise one another's bids, and demand turns the gathering into a thriving market.
- Active motifs: displaying an object for sale `quranic:root_000169:B002/m01`; she-camel selling briskly when offered `quranic:root_000176:B003/m01`; competitive bidding that asks for successive increases `quranic:root_000657:B004/m01`; market rising into active demand `quranic:root_001273:B018/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:37 `تِجَارَةٌ وَلَا بَيْعٌ ... إِقَامِ الصَّلَاةِ`; 24:38 `يَزِيدَهُم`; 24:46 `مُسْتَقِيمٍ`; 24:56 `أَقِيمُوا`
- Synthesis: Visible livestock, rival buyers, rising bids, and collective demand supply a concrete mechanism for the attention pressure resisted at 24:37. The adjacent `يَزِيدَهُم` at 24:38 is thereby reframed against another kind of increase: market escalation raises a price through competition, while divine increase follows worship that the market failed to capture and exceeds ordinary account.

### S16. [P3 24:35-46] Leaving Milk in the Udder Preserves the Next Yield
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A kneeling camel is milked in the morning, a remnant is deliberately left in the udder, milk returns during the interval, and the yield is collected without exhausting its source.
- Active motifs: morning milk drawn from a kneeling camel `quranic:root_000109:B007/m01`; milk left in the udder to call forth what follows `quranic:root_000478:B003/m01`; milk returning between two milkings `quranic:root_001188:B006/m01`; abundant or successive milk flow `quranic:root_000563:B006/m01`; small leather vessel for milk `quranic:root_000814:B004/m01`; milk depleted by overmilking or adulteration `quranic:root_000268:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 24:35 `مُبَارَكَةٍ ... مِشْكَاةٍ`; 24:40 forms of `فَوْق`; 24:47-52, 24:54, 24:56, 24:62-63 forms of `رَسُول`; 24:48, 24:51, 24:63 forms of `دَعَا`; 24:53 `جَهْدَ`; 24:61 `مُبَارَكَةً`
- Synthesis: Provision appears as renewable yield governed by interval and restraint. Leaving a remnant helps produce the next flow, whereas extracting to exhaustion destroys continuity. The scene materializes provision at 24:38 and usefully pressures the coercive worldly extraction forbidden at 24:33: immediate seizure and sustained productivity follow opposite operating rules.

### S17. [P4 24:47-64] A Fitted Pack Becomes Injury When Overloaded

- Ayah anchors: 24:29, 24:58, 24:60-61 forms of `جُنَاح`; 24:34 `مُتَّقِينَ`; 24:45 `بَطْنِهِ`; 24:52 `يَتَّقْهِ`; 24:53 `جَهْدَ`; 24:54 forms of `حُمِّلَ`
- Synthesis: The messenger's bounded burden at 24:54 becomes a mechanics of fit and capacity.
